why: All three must_catch items are handled. (1) Expect line 2 requires stderr to contain "the full path `<tmp>/c.json`... the line number `3` and the column number `3`", so the file path and the location are both required. (2) Return-{} is not an expect line. It is rejected in non_goals ("Making `loadConfig` swallow parse errors or return `{}`") and in assumptions ("That is not adopted: it hides the mistake..."). (3) Expect line 1 requires "exits with code 1 and prints nothing on stdout (in particular no `listening on` line)". Expect line 3 also requires that loadConfig throws instead of returning a value. Nothing in the output contradicts any of these items.
